department: College of Graduate Health Sciences — Biomedical Sciences Ph.D. (including Neuroscience track)

deadline.value: Priority deadline is December 1, 2026; final application deadline is March 1, 2027.

gre_general.value: The GRE is optional for Biomedical Sciences Ph.D. applicants.

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists for biomedical sciences or neurobiology, and the GRE is optional.

also.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: No prior supervisor is required; first-year students complete six 6-week laboratory rotations across tracks before choosing a research advisor by mutual consent.
supervisor.quote: Students are expected to complete a minimum number of laboratory rotations, determined by each track, to identify a research advisor. All tracks adhere to a schedule of six 6-week rotations periods that occur throughout the first year.

funding.value: Ph.D. students receive a $30,900 stipend plus payment of the health insurance premium (and CGHS GRA tuition waiver for up to six years).
funding.quote: Currently, students receive a stipend of $30,900 in addition to payment of the health insurance premium.

also.quote: During the first, and in some cases part of the second, year of study, The University of Tennessee Health Science Center provides a limited number of GRA appointments with stipends to qualified students; these are generally accompanied by a waiver of tuition and payment of the student’s health insurance premium for up to six years of study.

entry_route.value: A master's degree is not required; applicants need at least a bachelor's degree with a minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale.
entry_route.quote: No, but they should have at least a bachelor's degree with a documented grade-point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale from an accredited institution.

notes: Integrated Biomedical Sciences Ph.D. includes the Neuroscience concentration track (alongside Cancer & Developmental Biology, Genetics/Genomics/Informatics, Microbiology/Immunology/Biochemistry, Molecular & Translational Physiology, Pharmacology/Addiction Science/Toxicology, and Regenerative & Rehabilitation Sciences).
